rationale: A is better because it provides a more concrete, actionable funnel with explicit per-stage costs, disqualifiers, promotion evidence, task-specific comparison against the incumbent, and a detailed content-addressed cache for incremental retesting. Its honesty controls are also stronger and more internally aligned: pre-registered gates, automated scoring, non-negotiable kill criteria, cooling-off review, and visible near-misses. B has useful blind-review and audit-drift ideas, but its later stages undermine the stated weekly, single-machine constraint: a 4–8 hour deep evaluation and week-long production trial conflict with its claimed 2–4 GPU-hour cadence, and its Stage 3 rule—reject only when significantly worse on every dimension—can promote a candidate with serious regressions on several dimensions. A still has weaknesses, notably brittle single-probe rejection, limited statistical treatment of benchmark subsets, and inconsistent reject/watch wording, but its overall design is clearer, cheaper, and more operationally coherent.
